subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Nanotech in Diagnostics
description: A short lesson to help you apply DNA Nanotech in Diagnostics.

hook.text: A DNA tetrahedron sensor detects a single microRNA molecule in blood — early cancer biomarkers found with a DNA cage.

buildup.text: DNA nanostructures present capture probes at precise spacing — optimizing binding efficiency on sensor surfaces.

discovery.text: Electrochemical DNA sensors using tetrahedral probes achieve 1000-fold sensitivity improvement over flat DNA probes.

twist.text: The rigid 3D structure prevents probes from lying flat — every capture molecule stands upright and accessible.

climax.text: Point-of-care DNA nanostructure sensors are being tested — bringing lab-grade sensitivity to handheld devices.

punchline.text: A DNA cage stands probes upright — geometry boosts sensitivity a thousandfold.

quiz.question: Why do DNA tetrahedral probes outperform flat DNA probes in sensors?
options: Tetrahedral probes are made from different nucleotides
The rigid 3D structure keeps every capture probe upright and accessible, maximizing binding efficiency
Flat probes are destroyed by the sensor surface
